# dsh-imagegen

Image-generation and editing plugin for dsh: one `imagegen` tool that renders
and edits images throu

gh any OpenAI-compatible image backend, so agents can
generate and edit images without per-backend g

lue. The same tool lists the
configured routes, echoes the declared model lists, and live-probes the

ame tool lists the
configured routes, echoes the declared model lists, and live-probes the
backends.
## Tool verbs
| verb        | network | what it does |
| `generate`  | yes     | Generates the requested images. The tool writes the image files to disk an

d verifies each one is a PNG, JPEG, or WebP image. |
| `edit`      | yes     | Edits one or more exi
sting images: the tool reads the files named by the `images` argument (one entry per input image), p
osts them with the prompt to the backend, and writes the result files to disk with the same output h

andling as `generate`. |
| `providers` | no      | Lists the configured routes with their fields, th

e originating layer of each field, and the credential state. |
| `models`    | no      | Echoes the

declared model list of each route. The live model listing is the `status` verb. |
| `status`    | ye
s     | Probes each route's backend and reports reachability plus the live model list. |
Key `generate` and `edit` behaviors:

- The `prompt` argument is required for both verbs. For `edit`, the `images`
argument is also requir

ed (an array of one or more readable file paths).
- When the call omits `model`, the tool uses the r

oute's single declared
model. When a route declares no models, the tool asks the backend for its
mod

el list. When the declared or live model list contains several models,
the call fails and lists the

candidates.
- The tool passes `size` and `negativePrompt` to the backend as-is, and only
when the ca

ll sets them. The `seed` argument must be an integer, and the
tool passes it only when the call sets

it. The `n` argument is an integer
>= 1 with a default of 1, and a value greater than 1 requests a

batch.
- When the call sets `out`, the output path is that argument (a file path for
`n = 1`, or a d

irectory marked by a trailing separator or by existing on
disk). When the call omits `out`, the tool

writes the files to
`<process.cwd()>/images/<unixts>_<i>.<ext>`. The file extension matches
the ima

ge content type (`png` / `jpg` / `webp`).
- The tool verifies each written file is a PNG, JPEG, or W

ebP image. When it
is not, the call fails with `code: output`, and the tool keeps the file on
disk.

When the path cannot be written, the call fails the same way.

## Configuration

Providers are configured in any of four layers, lowest to highest priority;
the `providers` verb rep

orts the originating layer of every field, so a
shadowed value is never silent:

1. the built-in default (`api: openai-compatible`),
2. the `IMAGEGEN_*` env contract (static per pro

cess boot),
3. the cordis config layer (a patch entry with id `dsh-imagegen` and a
`config` object,

or profile-level patches),
4. the `dsh-imagegen:` section in the user settings document
(`$DSH_HOME/

settings.yaml`), which the plugin re-reads on every call, so
settings edits apply without a restart.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The env contract mirrors the config fields 1:1: `IMAGEGEN_DEFAULT_PROVIDER`,
and per route `<NAME>`

the variables `IMAGEGEN_PROVIDER_<NAME>_BASEURL`,
`IMAGEGEN_PROVIDER_<NAME>_API`, `IMAGEGEN_PROVIDER

_<NAME>_APIKEYENV`,
`IMAGEGEN_PROVIDER_<NAME>_HEADERS`, `IMAGEGEN_PROVIDER_<NAME>_MODELS`,
`IMAGEGEN

_PROVIDER_<NAME>_DISPLAYNAME`. The `<NAME>` segment is the route name
uppercased with `-` written as

`_`. The `headers` value is a JSON object
string, and the `models` value is a comma-separated list

of model ids. The
`baseURL` value is the OpenAI-compatible base URL including the `/v1` prefix
(the

same shape as an LLM provider base URL); the plugin appends
`/images/generations`, `/images/edits`,

and `/models` to it verbatim.
The `apiKeyEnv` value is a
reference to an environment variable name,

never a secret in config; per
request the value resolves from the process environment, then from
`$D
SH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`.

## Troubleshooting

A failing call returns the document `{ ok: false, error: { code, message,
provider?, elapsed_ms } }`

. The code set is `invalid_param` / `config` /
`network` / `timeout` / `http` / `protocol` / `output

The code set is `invalid_param` / `config` /
`network` / `timeout` / `http` / `protocol` / `output`.

- When a `config` error carries the message "no provider route is
configured", no route survived con

figuration. Check the base URLs; the tool
reports each route that configuration drops as a warning i

n the log.
- When a `config` error carries the message "credential missing: environment
variable "X"

is not set", the credential reference does not resolve. Set
`X` in the environment or add it to `$D

SH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`.
- When a `config` error carries the message "unknown provider "x"", the

route
name matches no configured route. Route names match case-insensitively and
treat `_` and `-` a

s the same separator; the error lists the configured
names.
- When a `config` error carries the mess

age "multiple providers configured
(...) and no default is set", pass the `provider` argument explic

itly, or
set `IMAGEGEN_DEFAULT_PROVIDER`, or set the settings `defaultProvider`.
- When an `output`

error carries the message "write failed", the tool could
not write to the `out` path. Check the dire

ctory and its permissions.
- When an `output` error carries the message "not a recognized image", th

e
backend returned bytes with no PNG, JPEG, or WebP magic. Inspect the kept
file; the backend may re

turn an unsupported container.
- When an `invalid_param` error from the `edit` verb names an `images

` path,
that file is absent or is not a regular file; pass readable image files.
- When an `edit` ca

ll fails with an `http` error and the message carries
status 400, the backend rejected the request;

a common cause is a `size`
the edit endpoint does not accept (some backends accept only
